reader.requirement: At --std 85, the word PIC is accepted wherever PICTURE is, with or without IS, in any clause position, and describes exactly the same item for every category of character-string (alphabetic, alphanumeric, numeric with S/V/P, numeric-edited); a PIC and a PICTURE in one entry are the same clause written twice.
reader.edition-search: The lexer rule is PIC : ('PIC' | 'PICTURE'), one token, with no mode or predicate; pictureClause is PIC IS? PIC_STRING with no edition predicate. Grepped CobolLexer.g4 and the pictureClause rule for edition predicates; the only edition-gated part of the clause is the 2002 LOCALE phrase (pictureLocalePhrase), not the keyword.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf11_04 covers X and ZZ9.99 strings with and without IS; signed, scaled (P), alphabetic, currency/CR edited and lower-case spellings are not exercised

probes.expected: each PIC/PICTURE pair (S9(3)V99, $$,$$9.99CR, A(3) incl. lower-case picture, COMP 9(5) after USAGE, PPP99) behaves identically
refused: PICT is not an abbreviation of PICTURE

probes.printed: error COBOL2423: the clause 'PIC X(3)' is written 2 times
probes.expected: PIC X(3) PICTURE X(3) is the one clause twice, refused

reader.notes: Equivalence is by construction: both spellings lex to the one PIC token, so no later stage can tell them apart, and the duplicate-clause screen treats them as one clause.
